I am 70 years old now, and my bones aren't what they used to be. I have farmed these five *mu* of land in Quzhou my whole life, and I know every corner of it. Around here, we follow the wheat-maize double-cropping system—that is what the land and the climate allow, and it is what I understand best. My wheat is already in the ground from last October; it is greening up now, so this spring I will topdress it with urea and irrigate it three more times after the winter irrigation I already gave it. I will also spray for weeds and aphids two or three times before harvest in early June. As soon as the wheat comes off, I will plant hybrid maize—Denghai 605—using no-tillage direct seeding, just like everyone else in the village. That saves me labor and time during the busy summer season. For the maize, I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate twice when the rains are not enough. I do not try new crops anymore; at my age, I want steady yields, familiar buyers, and manageable labor. The seeds, fertilizer, and pesticides I buy from the village cooperative, and I hire a machine for rotary tillage before the wheat. I expect about 1,000 *jin* per *mu* of wheat and a bit more from the maize if the weather cooperates.
